faq.a: Enter a whole number in decimal, binary, octal or hex and it shows all four bases at once at your chosen bit width (8, 16, 32 or 64). It also does bitwise AND, OR, XOR, NOT and left/right shift against a second value, computed with two's-complement wrapping at that width using BigInt, so large 64-bit values stay exact.

faq.q: How does the percent key behave?
faq.a: Percentages are rewritten before evaluation so everyday math works: 200 + 10% gives 220 and 200 − 10% gives 180 (the percentage is taken of the left-hand value), while 200 × 10% gives 20 and a standalone 50% becomes 0.5. This matters because calculators disagree on this — here the behaviour is explicit.

faq.q: What functions does Scientific mode support?
faq.a: Trig (sin, cos, tan and inverse/hyperbolic), ln, log10, log2, logn, sqrt, cbrt, nth root, powers, factorial, nPr, nCr, abs, floor, ceil, round and random. You switch between degrees and radians, there's a 2nd key for alternate functions, and a memory register with MC/MR/M+/M−/MS. Trig uses whichever angle mode is selected.

faq.q: Is it safe — does it use eval?
faq.a: No eval or new Function is used. Expressions are run through a real tokeniser and recursive-descent parser, which also means domain errors are caught with clear messages (for example sqrt of a negative, ln of zero, or division by zero). Results are rounded for display and the last 30 calculations are kept as a reusable history you can download as a tape.
